value.rationale: The two-arrow zero-composition locus is the natural variety of length-two chain complexes. Its all-frequency Fourier nonvanishing, exact divisibility in every characteristic/extension field, and sharp spectral inverse conditioning are structural spectral properties not supplied by a mere point count. The uniform q-adic rigidity across every pair of frequency matrices is the mechanism; no arbitrary slice or routine extension of a previous object is claimed. The result gives an exact invertibility law and optimal uniform Fourier inverse bound.
